summary: Follow-up call from Rohini Chitalekar (Chitrangan Kitchen Studio) on a website enquiry from Digambar Mandke for his new Flat 302 in Godavari Heights, Nashik Road. Kitchen is 8 x 10 ft, L-shaped, with a black granite slab already installed; he needs bottom trolleys and wall cabinets in BWR marine ply with acrylic shutters (Amrita model). Rohini quoted the standard ₹2.35 lakh before asking about budget; Digambar said his budget is ₹2 lakh and must stay within it. She immediately said it could be brought to ₹2 lakh by changing inner laminate and accessories, then added a ₹30,000 chimney and hob combo (₹2.65 lakh together). Delivery is three weeks after measurement and advance; possession is now 20 November (corrected from 15 November) with griha pravesh in December. Site visit booked for Saturday 24 October, 11:30 am, with senior designer Prasad Kulkarni; his wife Sunita Mandke will join to choose colours and handles. Warranty: 5 years on plywood, 10 years on hardware, in writing. Visit and 3D design are free; booking token ₹15,000, adjusted in the bill. Rohini will send the PDF catalog and photos on WhatsApp by 4 pm today.

strengths.title: Brought the wife into the decision and fitted his schedule
strengths.explanation: When Digambar said he can only do a weekend and that Sunita will choose colours and handles, you confirmed his Saturday 24 October 11:30 slot and welcomed her ('सुनीता madam सोबत असतील तर decision सोपा होईल'), promising physical sample folders. Keep treating the second decision-maker as a help, not a delay.

strengths.title: Solid scope discovery at the start
strengths.explanation: You checked the timing, referred to his enquiry, and asked new flat or renovation, size, layout and material needs. You learned the granite slab is already in place and only trolleys and cabinets are needed, which defines the real scope.

strengths.title: Concrete answers on warranty and charges
strengths.explanation: On his relative's bad after-sales experience you gave specifics: 5 years on BWR ply, 10 years on hardware, written warranty card with the tax invoice. Visit and 3D design free, ₹15,000 token adjusted in the bill. Specific numbers calm a cautious buyer better than general assurance.

improvements.title: Standard price quoted before budget or final scope
improvements.explanation: You quoted ₹2.35 lakh for the standard Amrita acrylic kitchen right after material choice, without asking his budget or which accessories he wants. He reacted that it was above his expectation and his budget is ₹2 lakh. Ask budget and must-haves first: 'Sir, या kitchen साठी तुम्ही साधारण किती budget ठरवलं आहे, आणि त्यात chimney-hob धरले आहेत का?'

improvements.title: Budget fit promised instantly, then the total went up
improvements.explanation: On his ₹2 lakh limit you said at once it can be done by changing inner laminate and accessories, without saying what he would give up. In the next answer you added the ₹30,000 combo and a ₹2.65 lakh total. The price story is now unclear. Explain the trade-off and let him choose, for example 'दोन लाखात बसवायचं असेल तर आतलं laminate आणि हे accessories बदलावे लागतील; designer visit मध्ये दोन्ही options दाखवतो.'

missed_opportunities.title: Did not check what the ₹2 lakh covers
missed_opportunities.explanation: When he asked about chimney and hob, you could have asked whether his ₹2 lakh includes appliances. That tells you if the real gap is ₹35,000 or ₹65,000.

missed_opportunities.title: Relative's bad service experience not explored
missed_opportunities.explanation: Digambar said a relative found nobody came back after problems. Your warranty answer was good, but asking what went wrong for the relative would let you address his exact fear, for example service response after installation.

missed_opportunities.title: Griha pravesh date not used to plan backwards
missed_opportunities.explanation: He mentioned griha pravesh in December and possession on 20 November. You proposed early measurement, which was good; also confirm the latest booking date that keeps the three-week schedule safely before the function.

objection_analysis.title: Price above budget: conceded too fast
objection_analysis.explanation: He said ₹2.35 lakh was more than expected and his budget is ₹2 lakh. You agreed to fit within budget without explaining the trade-offs, which may make him expect the same kitchen at ₹2 lakh.

objection_analysis.title: After-sales worry handled with specifics
objection_analysis.explanation: Written warranty with tenures and a warranty card with the invoice answered the concern directly.

objection_analysis.title: Appliances: gave him a choice
objection_analysis.explanation: You offered the ₹30,000 combo but also installation if he buys outside. He chose single-point responsibility himself. Good, low-pressure handling.

closing_analysis.title: Site visit booked with clear details
closing_analysis.explanation: Saturday 24 October, 11:30 am, at his flat, with Prasad Kulkarni and sample folders; repeated at the end. A clear, owned next step.

closing_analysis.title: Catalog commitment with a time
closing_analysis.explanation: You committed to send the Amrita PDF catalog and photos on his WhatsApp by 4 pm today so he can show Sunita in the evening. Meet that deadline; it is the first test of your reliability.

verdict: Warm, well-run follow-up that secured a site visit with both decision-makers. The weak spot is price: the standard quote came before budget, and the instant promise to fit ₹2 lakh followed by a ₹2.65 lakh total leaves the price expectation unclear for the visit.

dimensions.observation: Permission check, congratulations on the new flat and welcoming Sunita (s1, s5, s21) built a friendly base; written warranty specifics addressed his trust concern (s23).
Good scope discovery: new flat, 8 x 10 L-shape, granite in place, material needs (s3-s8). Budget and what it includes were not asked before pricing (s9-s10).
Budget (₹2 lakh) came only as a reaction to the quote (s10); timeline (possession 20 November, December griha pravesh) and joint decision with Sunita were identified (s16, s20).
Need is clear and practical: water-resistant ply, easy-clean acrylic, single responsibility for fitting (s8, s14). Little need to build pain; timing to the griha pravesh is the main driver (s16).
Amrita BWR ply with acrylic matched his stated needs (s7-s8). Price presentation was confusing: ₹2.35 lakh, then 'within ₹2 lakh', then ₹2.65 lakh with appliances (s9, s11, s13).
Warranty concern answered precisely (s23). Budget objection met with an unexplained concession (s11).
Visit booked on his preferred slot with designer and samples, catalog by 4 pm, token amount explained (s19, s25, s27). Final decision explicitly awaits Sunita (s20).
Wording is polite and positive, with clear read-backs of date and time (s19, s27). Tone of voice cannot be judged from text.

diagnosis.text: Strong rapport and a booked visit, but pricing was led by the list rate instead of the buyer's budget, leaving an unresolved ₹35,000 to ₹65,000 gap.

outcome.text: Site visit booked for Saturday 24 October at 11:30 am with designer Prasad Kulkarni; catalog to be sent on WhatsApp by 4 pm. No booking amount paid.

strength_details.why_it_matters: Colours and handles are Sunita's call; having her at the visit avoids a second round and shows respect for the family decision.
Knowing the slab is already done keeps the quote to cabinets and trolleys and avoids overpricing.
He cited a relative's bad experience; tenures in writing reduce that fear.

what_happened.text: ₹2.35 lakh was quoted straight after material choice; he replied his budget is ₹2 lakh.

improvement_details.why_it_matters: A list price before budget sets a number he now has to fight against, and the visit starts with a gap.
improvement_details.replacement_behavior: Ask budget and must-haves before any figure, then present a range that matches: 'तुमच्या budget मध्ये हे options बसतात...'

what_happened.text: You promised to reach ₹2 lakh by changing laminate and accessories, then gave a ₹2.65 lakh total with appliances.

improvement_details.why_it_matters: If the visit quote is higher than ₹2 lakh he may feel misled; if lower, the margin was given away without asking anything in return.
improvement_details.replacement_behavior: Name the trade-off and defer exact numbers to the visit: 'दोन लाखात बसवण्यासाठी काय बदलेल ते designer दोन options मध्ये दाखवतील.'

missing_inputs: Margin impact of the reduced specification

golden_moments.why_effective: Welcoming Sunita and promising physical samples turned a possible delay into a reason for the visit.
Specific tenures and a written card answered an emotional worry with facts.

prospect_signal.text: He asked whether chimney and hob are in the quote.

closer_response.text: You gave the ₹30,000 combo and a ₹2.65 lakh total without checking his budget's scope.

missed_details.follow_up: At the visit, ask whether ₹2 lakh is for cabinets only or including appliances.
missed_details.potential_impact: Sets the right target for the revised quote.

prospect_signal.text: He mentioned a relative whose vendor never came back after problems.

closer_response.text: You answered with warranty tenures and the warranty card.

missed_details.follow_up: Ask what happened in that case and explain how service requests are handled.
missed_details.potential_impact: Addresses the real fear behind the warranty question.

prospect_signal.text: Griha pravesh is in December; possession is 20 November.

closer_response.text: You proposed measuring now so installation can start right after 20 November.

missed_details.follow_up: State the last booking date that still finishes before the griha pravesh.
missed_details.potential_impact: Gives a genuine, non-pushy reason to decide soon after the visit.

source.text: He said ₹2.35 lakh was above his expectation and he must stay within ₹2 lakh.

prospect_interpretations.possible_concern: He may compare quotes and hold you to the ₹2 lakh you appeared to promise.

source.text: He said they will finalise only after discussing with Sunita.

prospect_interpretations.possible_concern: Design taste may decide more than price; samples at the visit will matter.

rewatch.text: Welcoming the spouse into the decision.

before.text: He asked about delivery time and gave possession and griha pravesh dates.

change.text: You proposed measuring now so installation can begin right after possession, and asked for a site visit.

after.text: He agreed to a visit and offered the Saturday 24 October slot.

conversation_change.possible_effect: Linking the visit to his own possession date may have made the visit feel useful rather than a sales push.

next_call_focus.behavior: Ask budget and what it includes before quoting any standard price.
next_call_focus.target: On the next enquiry call, the budget question comes before the first rupee figure.

practice.instructions: Prepare two budget questions in Marathi and practise moving from material choice to budget without quoting. Role-play a buyer who asks 'किती होईल?' early.
practice.success_condition: You respond with a budget question and a range tied to his answer, not the list price.

final_assessment.repeat: Bring every decision-maker into the visit and answer trust questions with specific, written terms.
final_assessment.fix_first: Get budget before price, and never promise to fit a budget without naming the trade-off.
final_assessment.next_focus: At the 24 October visit, present a clear option within ₹2 lakh and one full option, with appliances shown separately.
final_assessment.assessment: Good follow-up with a booked visit; price handling needs discipline.
